title: Times Tables to 12
subtitle: Factors 0 to 12
bounds: Factors 0 to 12. Forms: R a × b = ?, C a × ? = p, S ? × b = p (a missing factor is never 0). T1 R: the easy rows (0, 1, 2, 5, 10) and 11 times a digit, at least 8 with an 11 or 12 factor (117 prompts); T2 R: a 12 times 3, 4 or 9 (at least 6), 3-4-9 facts (at least 6), else a 3, 4 or 9 fact (33 prompts); T3 R: hard facts with an 11 or 12 (at least 8), 6-7-8 facts (at least 6), else a 6, 7 or 8 fact (37); T4 C: hard facts with an 11 or 12 (at least 6), 3-4-6-9 core facts (at least 8), else factors 2-12 (121); T5 S: hard facts with an 11 or 12 (at least 6), any hard fact with factors 3-12 (at least 6), plus C (at least 4 with an 11 or 12; 104 prompts in all). At most 6 prompts per tier with a 0 factor. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999. R: at least two within the larger factor of the answer (at least 2), at most one far; with a factor of 11 or more and an answer of 20 or more, one wrong value shares the answer's ones digit. C and S: at least two within 2 of the answer, at most one far. Answer ranks (smallest to largest of the four) each hold 15 to 35 percent of a tier.

tiers.name: Easy rows and 11s
tiers.description: Times 0, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 11, including the 11 and 12 rows.

tiers.name: Times 6, 7, 8, 12
tiers.description: Times 6, 7, 8 and 12. Split a factor, then add the parts.

tiers.name: Missing factors
tiers.description: Missing factor: 12 × ? = 84. Ask what times 12 makes 84.

tiers.name: Missing first factors
tiers.description: First factor missing: ? × 12 = 84, or a missing second factor. Factors up to 12.

GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

DROPPED_CARRY.student: Keep the ten: 13 × 6 is 60 + 18, and the 18 has a ten to add in.
DROPPED_CARRY.teacher: Splits into tens and ones but loses the ten from the ones product: 13 × 6 = 60 + 8 = 68.

TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Split into tens and ones, multiply each, add both.
TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones digit, tens place off by one ten (product plus or minus 10).

PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.student: Tens × tens plus ones × ones skips two parts. Split one number, multiply both.
PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.teacher: Multiplies tens by tens and ones by ones only: 13 × 14 = 100 + 12 = 112.

MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Check it: multiply your number by the shown one. Does it make the total?
MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing factor one too high or too low: counted the groups wrong, or never multiplied back to check.

MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Not subtraction. Ask: this number times what makes the total?
MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the shown factor from the product (p − k) instead of dividing the product by it.

MISSING_PRODUCT.student: The total is the product, not the missing factor. Multiply back to check.
MISSING_PRODUCT.teacher: Writes the product as the missing factor: the number already given in the equation.

items.explanation: 12 × 1 = 12: one group of 12. Any number times 1 is itself.
1 × 11 = 11: one group of 11. Any number times 1 is itself.
1 × 6 = 6: one group of 6. Any number times 1 is itself.
7 × 10 = 70: ten groups of 7, so put a zero after 7.

0 × 1 = 0: no groups, or groups of nothing, make 0. Anything times 0 is 0.
1 × 4 = 4: one group of 4. Any number times 1 is itself.

5 × 10 = 50: ten groups of 5, so put a zero after 5.
5 × 1 = 5: one group of 5. Any number times 1 is itself.
